title: feat: long-press "Replay Audio" action on message cells
body:
## Summary

Adds a **"Replay Audio"** option to the long-press context menu on message cells, letting users re-hear an assistant response without re-sending or scrolling to find the speaker controls.

### What changed

The existing `contextMenuConfigurationForRowAt` (which already offers "Branch conversation from here") now conditionally includes a second action:

```swift
if self?.messageHasReplayableAudio(message) == true {
    UIAction(title: "Replay Audio", image: "speaker.wave.2") { … }
}
```

- **`messageHasReplayableAudio(_:)`** — returns `true` when `role == "assistant"` and `SpeechSanitizer.sanitize(content)` is non-empty. This is the same sanitizer the live TTS path uses, so eligibility matches exactly what the voice pipeline can speak.
- Tapping the action calls `playMessageSynthesizer(message:)`, reusing the full existing TTS pipeline (Deepgram Aura-2 / ElevenLabs / OpenAI / AVSpeech offline fallback — respects mute state, speech speed, selected voice).
- The action is **hidden** for user messages, system messages, function-call messages, and assistant messages with empty/code-only content.
- Only one iOS message-cell surface exists (`MessagingVC`), so this covers all relevant iOS contexts.

### How to test manually

1. Open a conversation with at least one assistant reply.
2. Long-press an assistant message → context menu should show "Branch conversation from here" **and** "Replay Audio" (with `speaker.wave.2` icon).
3. Tap "Replay Audio" → the message's text is spoken via the active TTS provider.
4. Long-press a user message → only "Branch conversation from here" appears (no replay option).
5. Verify mute toggle is respected: mute, then replay → no audio plays.

### Tests

`LoopIOSTests/ReplayAudioEligibilityTests.swift` — unit tests for the eligibility logic (assistant with text → eligible; user/system/function/empty/code-only → ineligible).

### Limitations

- There is no cached audio per message — "Replay Audio" re-synthesizes via the TTS provider, so it requires an active API key (or falls back to offline AVSpeech). This matches the app's existing TTS architecture.
- The test target is not wired into the Xcode scheme yet (same as the other `LoopIOSTests` files).

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/960ec2bc609f4726807ef40c144b12f6
